calls.reason: The finite-element study demonstrates scientific uses, which Zitron explicitly allows. Civo describes hardware tradeoffs, but neither source establishes how substantial practical non-AI uses are across AI facilities.

Midjourney's founder reports profitability and a self-funded model, while Photoroom describes training its own model. Together these undermine the claim that AI startups inherently lose money through dependence on OpenAI and Anthropic.

The statement is explicitly hedged and its business-model conclusion is qualitative. SemiAnalysis reports better Blackwell tokens per dollar, challenging the cost premise without settling the broader inference.

Blackwell benchmark comparisons show lower estimated token costs. CoreWeave reports lower Rubin costs per Devin session, reinforced by NVIDIA's account of AgentX results; together they point against both parts, though cost details remain limited.

The FTC report makes no finding of coordinated cost deception. Washington Technology reports a competitor's procurement allegations, which do not establish the alleged conspiracy or its billing timeline.

Deloitte reports positive returns without complete deployment accounts. The randomized retailer study finds sales gains but explicitly lacks full cost data, leaving positive net ROI and the claimed cause of measurement difficulties unresolved.
